newsitem.title: USA: Immunity for tobacco not discussed -- Texas official.
newsitem.headline: Immunity for tobacco not discussed -- Texas official.

text.p: Texas Attorney General Dan Morales said on Tuesday a proposal to grant tobacco companies future legal protection in exchange for a settlement of the many lawsuits against them was not under discussion in negotiations now underway.
Morales told reporters he was willing to listen to proposals granting tobacco firms limited immunity for past alleged misdeeds, but not the future.
"This issue of immunity for the industry is no longer on the table and you may strike that from any discussion of future negotiatons," he said in a news conference.
Morales the attorneys general from the 24 states who have filed tobacco lawsuits "are united on this issue of immunity."

News reports have said the tobacco industry, in settlement talks with anti-smoking groups, has proposed putting up to $300 billion into a fund to reimburse states for Medicaid costs linked to smoking. In return, cigarette makers would reportedly ask for broad protection from lawsuits.
But Morales said $300 billion "is not sufficient" for a settlement. When asked how much it would take to reach a settlement, Morales replied: "Well in excess of $300 billion."
